exposure: Mode of birth (C-section vs. vaginal delivery)
Human milk feeding patterns (exclusive, predominant, partial)
Detection of maternal stool B. infantis
outcome: Absolute abundance of B. infantis in infant stool
Absolute abundance of B. longum in infant stool
Absolute abundance of B. breve in infant stool
Patterns of postnatal Bifidobacterium subspecies colonization
Timing of emergence of B. infantis
cohort: The study included stool samples from 1132 infants aged 0-6 months from urban Dhaka, Bangladesh.
finding: B. infantis absolute abundance started low at birth but increased in the first two months, whereas B. longum and B. breve abundances remained comparatively low, and infant antibiotic exposure, human milk feeding patterns, and detection of maternal stool B. infantis were not associated with infant B. infantis.
mod_finding: B. infantis emerged earlier in infants delivered by C-section, but by approximately 2 months of age, infants delivered by C-section or vaginally had similar B. infantis absolute abundances.
